title: And, inclusive or and exclusive or

draft.title: And, inclusive or and exclusive or
card: A happens, or B happens, or both happen.
One of A and B happens, but not both.
Example: roll a die. A is an even number and B is a number above 3. A and B: 4, 6. Inclusive A or B: 2, 4, 5, 6. Exclusive A or B: 2, 5.
draft.remember: Both is and. Either or both is inclusive or. Just one is exclusive or.

a.q: A die is rolled. A is an even number and B is a number above 3. Which outcomes are in A and B?
a.why: A and B needs both: even and above 3, which gives 4 and 6. The list 2, 4, 5 and 6 is tempting, but it is inclusive or, where one is enough.
a.clue: The number must pass both tests.

b.q: In a class of 10 students, 4 play netball and 5 play soccer. 2 play both. How many play exactly one of the two sports?
b.why: Only netball is 4 − 2 = 2 and only soccer is 5 − 2 = 3, so exclusive or gives 2 + 3 = 5. The answer 7 is inclusive or, which counts the 2 who play both once.
b.clue: Remove the students who play both.

check.summary: No problems found. The card's die example, both answers and both explanations check out: A and B is 4 and 6, and 2 + 3 = 5 students play exactly one sport.
